about.title: About TAK
about.whatIsTakText: Tak is an abstract strategy game designed by James Ernest and Patrick Rothfuss. It was first introduced in Patrick Rothfuss's fantasy novel "The Wise Man's Fear" as a fictional game, and later brought to life as a real board game.
about.howToPlayText: The goal of Tak is to create a road - a connected line of your pieces that spans from one edge of the board to the opposite edge. Players take turns placing and moving pieces on the board.
about.flatStonesDesc: Basic pieces that can form roads
about.wallsDesc: Standing stones that block roads and movement
about.capstonesDesc: Special pieces that can flatten walls and form roads
about.createRoad: Create a road connecting opposite edges
about.mostFlats: Have the most flat stones when the board is full
about.firstTurnText: Each player's first move must place an opponent's flat stone. This ensures a more balanced opening.
about.stackMovementText: You can pick up and move stacks of pieces, dropping them along orthogonal paths. The carry limit equals the board size.
